title: Factorized task-dependence locus code in a three-stage linear recurrent cell
hypothesis: A compact task factor times a discrete input/recurrent/readout locus code recovers held-out task functions and identifies which computational locus carries task dependence, with fewer complete bytes than independent task matrices.
insertion: one rank-1 additive update at exactly one of input, recurrent, or readout linear maps; task code stores scalar factor and locus ID

task_grid.heldout: all three +1 tasks; fit only -1 and 0 examples per locus

development.tuning: none; fixed rank-1 updates and linear task coordinates

fresh.release_rule: Do not open fresh after native low-rank alias or failed frozen gate.

controls: independent full layer matrices per task
shared three-stage core without task code
native rank-1 low-rank conditional update at the same locus

paid: rank-1 left/right vectors for each locus

pass_gate: Heldout output nRMSE <=0.02, >=25% fewer bytes than independent, locus ablation identifies the generating locus, and strict storage/compute/quality advantage over native low-rank conditional control.
fail_gate: FAIL Mirror-specific claim for exact native low-rank alias, quality miss, or no native-control frontier gain.

compute.active_MACs: three dense base maps plus one rank-1 update (2D) per example
compute.reconstruction_MACs: rank-1 update materialization for all task/locus entries, reported separately

boundaries: Synthetic linear three-stage function screen, not a trained RNN or task benchmark.
Task factor and locus label are supplied and charged; no task inference claim.
Heldout positive scalar tasks are extrapolated from -1 and 0 using the preregistered linear coordinate rule.
Native low-rank is deliberately parameter matched to the View.
